questions.question: In May 2025, which advanced research facility was inaugurated by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) with the aim to further strengthen indigenous quantum capabilities for strategic and defence applications?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Quantum Technology Research Centre, Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **May 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** reached a significant milestone by inaugurating the **Quantum Technology Research Centre** located in **Delhi**.
 
• The primary objective of this advanced research facility is to strengthen **indigenous quantum capabilities** specifically tailored for **strategic and defence applications**, ensuring **national security** in an evolving technological landscape.
 
• The centre is dedicated to developing cutting-edge technologies such as **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)**, **Quantum Communication**, and **Quantum Sensing** to provide secure data transmission and advanced detection systems for the armed forces.
 
• This initiative aligns with the vision of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) by reducing dependency on foreign technologies for sensitive **cryptographic** and **surveillance** equipment.
 
• The facility acts as a hub for scientists and researchers to collaborate on **quantum computing** algorithms that can solve complex logistical and strategic problems much faster than classical computers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, it is the R&D wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, it oversees a network of more than **50 laboratories** developing diverse technologies in **aeronautics**, **armaments**, **electronics**, and **missile systems**.
 
• The organization plays a pivotal role in maintaining the **technological edge** of the Indian Military through local innovation.
 
 
 
• **National Quantum Mission (NQM):**
 
 
• Approved by the Union Cabinet in **2023** with a total outlay of over **Rs. 6,000 crore**.
 
• The mission aims to seed, nurture, and scale up scientific and industrial R&D in **Quantum Technology (QT)** over the next **eight years**.
 
• It targets the development of **intermediate-scale quantum computers** with **50-1000 physical qubits** in various platforms.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Quantum Tech:**
 
 
• **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)**: Allows two parties to produce a shared random secret key known only to them, which can be used to encrypt and decrypt messages, making them immune to **hacking**.
 
• **Quantum Radar**: Utilizes quantum entanglement to detect **stealth aircraft** and objects that are otherwise invisible to conventional radar systems.
 
• **Precision Timing**: Quantum clocks provide highly accurate time synchronization, which is critical for **GPS** and **navigation systems** during wartime.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geospatial Advantage:** Establishing the centre in **Delhi** facilitates seamless coordination between **DRDO Headquarters**, the **Ministry of Defence**, and academic powerhouses like **IIT Delhi**.
 
• **Future Readiness:** The **May 2025** inauguration signifies India's commitment to staying ahead in the **global quantum race**, which is currently dominated by nations like the **USA** and **China**.
 
• **Indigenous Development:** Most of the hardware and software protocols developed at the **Quantum Technology Research Centre** are built from the ground up to prevent **backdoor vulnerabilities** in military hardware.
 
• **Dual-use Nature:** While the primary focus is **defence**, the breakthroughs achieved here in **quantum sensors** can also be applied to **civilian sectors** like healthcare and disaster management.
</ul

questions.question: Which country became the first team to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup (excluding host nations)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Japan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Japan** officially became the first nation to qualify for the **2026 FIFA World Cup** through the qualification process, excluding the three host nations who receive automatic berths.
 
• The "Samurai Blue" secured their mathematical qualification on **March 20, 2025**, following a decisive victory in the **AFC (Asian Football Confederation) Third Round** of qualifiers.
 
• Competing in **Group C** of the Asian qualifiers, **Japan** maintained a dominant run under the management of head coach **Hajime Moriyasu**, ensuring a top-two finish in their group with several games to spare.
 
• This achievement marks **Japan's 8th consecutive** appearance in the **FIFA World Cup**, a streak that began in **1998** when the tournament was held in **France**.
 
• The qualification was confirmed after **Japan** accumulated enough points to be beyond the reach of the third-placed team in their qualifying group, effectively utilizing the expanded **8.5 slots** allocated to **Asia** for the upcoming tournament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **2026 FIFA World Cup Expansion:**
 
 
• The **2026** edition will be the first to feature **48 teams**, an increase from the **32-team** format used since **1998**.
 
• This expansion allows more teams from **Asia (AFC)**, **Africa (CAF)**, and **North America (CONCACAF)** to participate in the global event.
 
 
 
• **Host Nations:**
 
 
• The tournament will be historically unique as it is co-hosted by three countries: the **United States**, **Canada**, and **Mexico**.
 
• All three host nations qualify **automatically** and are not required to participate in the regional qualification rounds.
 
 
 
• **Other AFC Contenders:**
 
 
• **South Korea**: Holds the record for the most World Cup appearances by an **Asian** nation (**11 times**) and was among the next teams to qualify shortly after **Japan**.
 
• **Iran**: Known as "Team Melli," they are a powerhouse in **West Asia** and have been consistent qualifiers in recent cycles (**2014, 2018, 2022**).
 
• **Australia**: After moving from the **OFC** to the **AFC** in **2006**, the "Socceroos" have qualified for every tournament, often through intense **inter-continental play-offs**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tournament Timeline:** The **2026 FIFA World Cup** is scheduled to take place from **June 11** to **July 19, 2026**.
 
• **Venues:** A total of **16 cities** across the three host countries will host matches, with the final match set to be played at **MetLife Stadium** in **East Rutherford, New Jersey**.
 
• **Qualification Slots:** The **AFC** received a significant boost in slots, moving from **4.5** to **8.5**, which facilitated the early qualification of top-tier teams like **Japan**.
 
• **Historical Context:** **Mexico** will become the first country to host or co-host the **FIFA World Cup** three times, having previously hosted in **1970** and **1986**.
</ul

questions.question: The Railways ordered which safety feature to be installed at stations in Pune in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panic alert buttons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Railways** has issued a directive to install **Panic alert buttons** at various railway stations within the **Pune Division** to enhance passenger security, with a target completion date of **June 2025**.
 
• These buttons are specifically designed to act as an emergency signaling system for **women**, **children**, and **elderly passengers** who may find themselves in distress while on the platform.
 
• The system is directly integrated with the **Railway Protection Force (RPF)** control room; once the button is pressed, an alert is instantly generated, identifying the **exact location** of the passenger.
 
• This safety feature is part of the **Indian Railways'** ongoing efforts to modernize **station infrastructure** and provide a proactive response mechanism against crimes like **harassment** or **theft**.
 
• The initiative in **Pune** serves as a critical pilot for implementing **IoT-based security solutions** that bridge the gap between passengers and security personnel in real-time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pune Railway Division**: Falling under the **Central Railway** zone, it is one of the highest revenue-generating and busiest divisions in **Maharashtra**, making it a priority for safety upgrades.
 
• **Integrated Security System (ISS)**: The **Panic alert buttons** are a component of the broader **ISS**, which also includes **CCTV surveillance**, **baggage scanners**, and **metal detectors** to provide multi-layered protection.
 
• **Railway Protection Force (RPF)**: A specialized security force under the **Ministry of Railways**, the **RPF** is tasked with the protection of **railway property** and the safety of the **42 crore** (approximate) annual passengers using the network.
 
• **Meri Saheli Initiative**: This program works alongside physical safety features like buttons, where dedicated teams of **female RPF personnel** interact with solo women travelers to provide security throughout their journey.
 
• **Nirbhaya Fund**: Many such safety installations at **Indian Railways** stations are funded through the **Nirbhaya Fund**, a non-lapsable corpus established in **2013** for schemes aimed at improving **women's safety** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Response Mechanism**: Upon activation of the button, **Quick Reaction Teams (QRT)** of the **RPF** are expected to reach the spot within **3 to 5 minutes** to assist the passenger.
 
• **Technological Features**: Most modern **Panic alert buttons** installed by the railways are equipped with **two-way communication**, allowing the passenger to speak directly with the dispatcher while help is on the way.
 
• **Timeline**: The **June 2025** deadline set for **Pune** stations ensures that the technology is synced with the **Smart City** projects currently being implemented in the region.
 
• **Legal Context**: Under the **Railways Act, 1989**, ensuring the safety of passengers is a statutory duty, and the introduction of such devices helps the administration meet these legal and **ethical obligations**.
</ul

questions.question: From March 9 to 12, 2025, the second part of India's fifth Khelo India Winter Games was conducted in which of the following places?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulmarg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **second part** of the **5th edition** of the **Khelo India Winter Games (KIWG)** was scheduled to be held in **Gulmarg**, situated in the **Baramulla district** of **Jammu and Kashmir**.
 
• This second leg of the prestigious national event took place from **March 9 to 12, 2025**, featuring high-adrenaline snow sports.
 
• While the **Gulmarg** phase focused on mountain-based activities, the **first part** of the **2025** games was hosted in **Leh**, **Ladakh**, between **January 30 and February 2, 2025**.
 
• The events conducted during the **Gulmarg** leg primarily included **Alpine Skiing**, **Snowboarding**, **Ski Mountaineering**, and **Nordic Skiing**.
 
• The games are a collaborative effort between the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)**, and the **J&K Sports Council** to promote winter sports culture in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gulmarg as a Sports Hub**: 
 
 
• Known as the "Meadow of Flowers," **Gulmarg** is one of the world's premier **ski destinations** located at an altitude of approximately **2,650 meters** in the **Pir Panjal Range** of the **Himalayas**.
 
• It has hosted the majority of the **Khelo India Winter Games** editions since their inception due to its world-class slopes at **Kongdoori** and **Mary Shoulder**.
 
 
 
• **Khelo India Winter Games (KIWG) History**: 
 
 
• The **first edition** of the **KIWG** was held in **2020**. It was launched to identify and nurture talent for international winter sports competitions like the **Winter Olympics**.
 
• The **4th edition** in **2024** also followed a dual-venue format between **Ladakh** and **Jammu & Kashmir**, where **Army Sports Control Board (ASCB)** topped the medal tally.
 
 
 
• **Broad Objective of Khelo India**: 
 
 
• The **Khelo India program** was introduced in **2018** by the **Government of India** to revive the sports culture at the grass-root level by building a strong framework for all sports played in the country.
 
• It encompasses various verticals including **Khelo India Youth Games**, **University Games**, and **Winter Games**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sports Disciplines**: The **5th KIWG** included diverse disciplines. While **Leh** hosted **Ice Hockey** and **Speed Skating**, the **Gulmarg** leg was dedicated to snow-dependent sports.
 
• **Mascot and Symbolism**: The mascot for the games typically features the **Snow Leopard** (often named **'Sheen-e-She'** in local dialect), which symbolizes the **Himalayan heritage** and the spirit of resilience.
 
• **National Participation**: Hundreds of athletes from various **States**, **Union Territories**, and **Central Boards** participate, fostering national integration through sports.
 
• **Tourism Impact**: Hosting these games in **2025** significantly boosts **winter tourism** in **Jammu & Kashmir** and **Ladakh**, positioning India as a global winter sports destination.
</ul

questions.question: According to Union Budget 2025–26, approximately _______ was allocated for the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹3,413 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025–26** has allocated approximately **₹3,413 crore** to the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** to bolster India's ecological and environmental initiatives.
 
• This allocation is pivotal for implementing the **National Mission for a Green India**, which aims at protecting, restoring, and enhancing India's diminishing forest cover and responding to **climate change**.
 
• A significant portion of this fund is dedicated to **Control of Pollution**, supporting the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** to reduce particulate matter concentration in **131 cities** across the country.
 
• The budget also provides financial support to statutory and autonomous bodies under the ministry, such as the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** and the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)**.
 
• Funding for **Project Tiger** and **Project Elephant** is integrated into this allocation to ensure the conservation of India's **megafauna** and their natural habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• It is the nodal agency in the administrative structure of the **Central Government** for the planning, promotion, and coordination of India's environmental and forestry policies.
 
• The ministry was established in **1985** and is currently headed by the **Union Minister of Environment**.
 
• It oversees the implementation of major acts like the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** and the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
 
 
• **Budgetary Framework in India:**
 
 
• The **Union Budget** is the **Annual Financial Statement** of the country, presented under **Article 112** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• The budget for **2025-26** was presented by the **Union Finance Minister**, **Nirmala Sitharaman**, on **February 1, 2025**.
 
• Budgetary allocations reflect the government's priorities, such as the **Net Zero by 2070** commitment made at **COP26**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Climate Action and Mission LiFE:** The budget supports **Mission LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment)**, a global movement aimed at individual and community action to protect the environment.
 
• **Coastal Management:** Funds are also earmarked for the **Integrated Coastal Zone Management** project to conserve marine biodiversity and improve the livelihoods of **coastal communities**.
 
• **Circular Economy:** There is an increased focus on **waste management** and **circular economy** principles to ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns.
 
• **Ramsar Sites:** The allocation assists in the maintenance of **Wetlands of International Importance**, helping India fulfill its obligations under the **Ramsar Convention**.

questions.question: What is the name of DRDO's homegrown multi-layered defense system, showcased for the first time at the 2025 Republic Day parade and Aero India 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rakshak-Suraksha Kavach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rakshak-Suraksha Kavach** is an advanced, homegrown **multi-layered air defense system** developed by the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** to provide comprehensive protection against a variety of aerial threats.
 
• This sophisticated system made its debut appearance at the **76th Republic Day Parade** held on **January 26, 2025**, at **Kartavya Path**, **New Delhi**, showcasing India’s growing prowess in defense manufacturing.
 
• It was also a major highlight at **Aero India 2025**, the **15th edition** of the biennial air show held at the **Yelahanka Air Force Station** in **Bengaluru**, **Karnataka**.
 
• The **Rakshak-Suraksha Kavach** is designed to integrate various existing and new missile systems into a single **Command and Control (C2)** architecture, creating a "seamless shield" for the country's critical infrastructure and airspace.
 
• The system is specifically engineered to detect, track, and neutralize threats such as **ballistic missiles**, **cruise missiles**, **fighter jets**, and **unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)** or **drone swarms** at multiple ranges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**
 
 
• Established in **1958**, **DRDO** is the R&D wing of the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India, with its headquarters in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is responsible for the design and development of state-of-the-art **defense technologies**, including **missiles**, **armored vehicles**, **radars**, and **electronic warfare systems**.
 
 
 
• **Aero India 2025:**
 
 
• This event is Asia’s largest **aerospace and defense exhibition**, providing a platform for **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) to demonstrate its **indigenous aviation** and **aerospace capabilities**.
 
• The **2025** edition focused on the **Viksit Bharat @ 2047** vision, emphasizing the export potential of Indian-made defense hardware to the global market.
 
 
 
• **Multi-Layered Defense Architecture:**
 
 
• A multi-layered system typically consists of **Very Short Range Air Defence (VSHORAD)** for close-in protection, **Medium Range Surface-to-Air Missiles (MRSAM)**, and **Long Range** interceptors.
 
• The **Kavach** system acts as the central nervous system that synchronizes **radars** and **launchers** to ensure zero-gap security.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Features:** The **Rakshak-Suraksha Kavach** utilizes **Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA)** radars for **360-degree surveillance** and **precision tracking** of high-speed targets.
 
• **Strategic Significance:** The deployment of this homegrown system reduces **India's** dependency on foreign air defense platforms like the **S-400 Triumf** from **Russia** or the **Iron Dome** from **Israel**.
 
• **Collaboration:** The project involved collaboration between **DRDO**, various **Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs)** like **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**, and private industry partners under the **Make in India** initiative.
 
• **Modern Warfare Adaptation:** The inclusion of **anti-drone** modules within the **Kavach** system highlights its readiness for **asymmetric warfare** and **cyber-electronic** threats prevalent in modern conflicts.
</ul

questions.question: What happens if the accused minister (Prime Minister / Chief Minister) is granted bail within 30 days according to the Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025?

options.text: They are automatically disqualified for 5 years.
They are removed from office permanently.
No action is taken; they can continue in office.
They are suspended from their post for 30 more days.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No action is taken; they can continue in office**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025**, introduces specific provisions regarding the administrative continuity of the **Prime Minister** and **Chief Ministers** in the event of their arrest or legal detention.
 
• According to the bill, if an accused minister, such as the **Prime Minister** or a **Chief Minister**, is granted **bail** within a window of **30 days** from the date of arrest, **no action is taken** against their position.
 
• This ensures that the individual can **continue in office** and perform their constitutional duties without being subjected to automatic **suspension** or **disqualification**, provided the legal stay is brief.
 
• The bill aims to balance the legal rights of the **accused** with the necessity of maintaining stability in the executive branch of the **government**.
 
• If the individual fails to secure **bail** within the stipulated **30-day** period, the bill prescribes further consequences, but the immediate **30-day** period serves as a protective grace window.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 368:** The **Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025**, would be processed under **Article 368** of the **Constitution of India**, which grants **Parliament** the power to amend the document through a **Special Majority**.
 
• **Representation of the People Act, 1951:** Historically, **Section 8** of this **Act** deals with the **disqualification** of representatives upon **conviction**. However, the new **2025 amendment** specifically addresses the status of ministers at the **accused** stage before a final verdict is reached.
 
• **Governance Continuity:** The bill addresses the recent legal and political debates in **India** (observed in cases during **2023** and **2024**) concerning whether a **Chief Minister** can run the **government** from judicial custody.
 
• **Judicial Custody vs. Police Custody:** The **30-day** limit applies regardless of whether the official is in **police custody** or **judicial custody**, emphasizing the availability of **bail** as the determining factor for continuing in office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **30-Day Threshold:** The **numerical value** of **30 days** is critical; it serves as a legislative compromise to prevent the **misuse** of investigative agencies to topple **governments** through short-term arrests.
 
• **Executive Stability:** The provision that **no action is taken** reflects the principle that the mandate of the **electorate** should not be subverted by mere allegations unless the detention is prolonged enough to hinder **governance**.
 
• **Role of the President and Governor:** Under this bill, the **President** (for the **PM**) and the **Governor** (for the **CM**) are required to wait for the expiration of the **30-day** period before initiating any constitutional process for **suspension** or replacement.
 
• **Legal Precedents:** This amendment seeks to codify matters that were previously left to judicial interpretation by the **Supreme Court** or the **High Courts** regarding the "morality" of holding office while under **arrest**.
</ul

questions.question: Who is the author of the Lithuanian novel, ‘The Last Day’, which was translated into Hindi by the Sahitya Akademi in October 2025 as part of celebrating literary exchange and cultural collaboration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaroslavas Melnikas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jaroslavas Melnikas** is the celebrated author of the **Lithuanian** novel titled **‘The Last Day’** (originally published as **‘Paskutinė diena’**).
 
• The **Hindi translation** of this novel was released by the **Sahitya Akademi** in **October 2025** as a landmark step in fostering **literary exchange** and **cultural collaboration** between **India** and **Lithuania**.
 
• The novel is a profound **philosophical work** that explores a world where every human being knows the **exact date of their death**, challenging the reader to reflect on the value of life and time.
 
• This translation is part of a broader initiative by the **Ministry of Culture** and **Sahitya Akademi** to bring **contemporary European literature** to Indian readers in their native languages.
 
• By translating works from the **Baltic region** into **Hindi**, the project aims to deepen the **bilateral cultural ties** and provide a platform for modern **Lithuanian voices** in the **Indian subcontinent**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jaroslavas Melnikas:**
 
 
• Born in **1959**, he is a prominent **Lithuanian-Ukrainian** writer, critic, and philosopher.
 
• His works are known for their **existentialist themes** and have been translated into numerous languages, including **French**, **English**, and **German**.
 
• He has received several prestigious literary awards, and his novel **‘The Last Day’** was a finalist for the **Book of the Year** in **Lithuania**.
 
 
 
• **Sahitya Akademi:**
 
 
• Established on **12 March 1954**, it is India’s **National Academy of Letters**.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi** promotes literature in **24 Indian languages** and frequently engages in **international translation projects** to promote global literary harmony.
 
• It is headquartered at **Rabindra Bhavan** in **New Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **India-Lithuania Cultural Relations:**
 
 
• The cultural connection between the two nations is historically significant due to the **linguistic similarities** between **Lithuanian** and **Sanskrit**.
 
• Translating modern fiction like **‘The Last Day’** helps modernize this ancient connection by showcasing **21st-century** thought and creativity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Distinguished Lithuanian Authors (Options Analysis):**
 
 
• **Vincas Mykolaitis-Putinas:** A legendary **20th-century** poet and novelist, most famous for his psychological novel **‘In the Shadow of Altars’** (1933).
 
• **Jurga Ivanauskaitė:** A modern writer and **activist** (1961–2007) known for her work **‘The Witch and the Rain’** and her deep interest in **Tibetan Buddhism**.
 
• **Balys Sruoga:** A famous playwright and poet known for the memoir **‘The Forest of the Gods’**, which details his survival in a **Stutthof concentration camp**.
 
 
 
• **Translation Significance:**
 
 
• Translating into **Hindi**, one of the **most spoken languages** in the world, ensures that **Jaroslavas Melnikas’s** unique vision reaches a massive audience, enriching the **Indian literary landscape**.

questions.question: Which of the following bilateral agreements was signed between India and Singapore and marked the upgrade of their relationship by exchanging several MoUs in areas such as semiconductors, digital technologies and skills development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **September 2024**, during the official visit of Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** to **Singapore**, the bilateral relationship between the two nations was officially elevated to a **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**.
 
• This upgrade marks a significant evolution from the **Strategic Partnership** that was established in **2015**, reflecting the deepening trust and widening scope of cooperation.
 
• The two countries signed and exchanged several **Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs)** focusing on critical future-oriented sectors: **Semiconductors**, **Digital Technologies**, **Skill Development**, and **Healthcare**.
 
• The **Semiconductor ecosystem partnership** is particularly noteworthy, as it aims to leverage **Singapore’s** established global role in semiconductor manufacturing to support **India’s** nascent but ambitious semiconductor industry.
 
• The agreements were exchanged in the presence of PM **Narendra Modi** and Singapore’s Prime Minister **Lawrence Wong**, emphasizing a shared vision for a stable and prosperous **Indo-Pacific** region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Synergy:** **Singapore** has consistently been one of the largest sources of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** for **India**, with cumulative investments exceeding **$160 billion** since **2000**.
 
• **CECA (2005):** The **Comprehensive Economic Cooperation Agreement (CECA)**, signed in **2005**, was **India’s** first-ever comprehensive trade agreement with any country, facilitating easier trade in goods, services, and investments.
 
• **Digital Connectivity:** In **February 2023**, **India** and **Singapore** launched the linkage of their real-time payment systems—**UPI** and **PayNow**—enabling faster and cheaper cross-border remittances.
 
• **Defense Cooperation:** The maritime relationship is anchored by the **SIMBEX** (Singapore-India Maritime Bilateral Exercise), which has been held annually since **1994**, making it one of **India's** longest-running naval exercises with any foreign country.
 
• **Historical Ties:** **India** was among the first countries to recognize **Singapore** as an independent nation in **1965**, and both nations will celebrate the **60th anniversary** of diplomatic relations in **2025**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable (ISMR):** This high-level mechanism, established in **2022**, played a crucial role in identifying the new pillars of the **Comprehensive Strategic Partnership**, including **Food Security**, **Green Energy**, and **Advanced Manufacturing**.
 
• **Skill Development Focus:** The **MoU on Educational Cooperation and Skill Development** aims to collaborate on vocational training and **Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET)** to enhance the employability of the Indian workforce.
 
• **Healthcare Collaboration:** The partnership in **Healthcare and Medical Research** focuses on pandemic preparedness, genomic surveillance, and digital health solutions to tackle emerging global health challenges.
 
• **Sustainability:** Both nations are working closely under the **Green Economy** framework to promote sustainable finance, **Green Hydrogen**, and carbon credit collaborations.

questions.question: Which state hosted the Khelo India Youth Games, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The state of **Bihar** has been officially selected to host the **7th edition** of the **Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG)** in **2025**.
 
• This announcement was made by the **Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports**, **Shri Mansukh Mandaviya**, during a meeting with state sports ministers, signifying a major shift in hosting national events in the eastern part of India.
 
• It will be the **first time** in history that **Bihar** will host this prestigious national multi-sport competition, highlighting the state’s growing commitment to developing **sports infrastructure** and talent.
 
• The **2025** edition aims to provide a platform for approximately **7,000 to 8,000 athletes** from across the country to compete in various sporting disciplines.
 
• The **Government of Bihar** is expected to utilize venues in **Patna** and other districts to conduct the games, promoting a sports culture at the **grassroots level** within the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Previous Edition (2024):**
 
 
• The **6th edition** of the **Khelo India Youth Games** was hosted by **Tamil Nadu** in **January 2024**.
 
• The games were held across four cities: **Chennai**, **Madurai**, **Trichy**, and **Coimbatore**.
 
• **Maharashtra** emerged as the overall champion of the **2024** games, securing the top spot in the medal tally.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of KIYG:**
 
 
• The **Khelo India Youth Games** (formerly known as **Khelo India School Games**) were launched in **2018** by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• The inaugural edition was held in **New Delhi**, and since then, it has become the biggest talent-identification platform in Indian sports.
 
• The games are organized in two categories: **under-17 years** for school students and **under-21 years** for college and university students.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of Khelo India:**
 
 
• The primary objective of the **Khelo India** initiative is to revive the **sports culture** in India by integrating sports with the education system and identifying talent at a young age.
 
• Selected athletes receive an annual financial assistance of **Rs. 5 lakh** for a period of **8 years** to prepare for international competitions, including the **Olympics**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Maharashtra** and **Haryana** have been the most successful states in the history of the **Khelo India Youth Games**, often alternating for the top position in the medal table.
 
• In the **2024** edition, **Silambam** (a traditional martial art of **Tamil Nadu**) was featured as a **demo sport** for the first time.
 
• The hosting of the **2025** games in **Bihar** is part of the **"Sports for All"** vision, ensuring that states with untapped potential get the opportunity to upgrade their facilities and showcase local talent.
 
• The **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** uses a **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** in conjunction with **Khelo India** to ensure the best young athletes receive world-class training and exposure.
</ul

questions.question: Which Ukrainian city suffered a deadly Russian missile strike in mid-June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dnipro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **mid-June 2025**, the city of **Dnipro** in central **Ukraine** was the site of a devastating **Russian missile strike** that targeted both civilian infrastructure and residential complexes.
 
• The attack involved the use of **high-precision cruise missiles**, which struck a multi-story apartment building and a nearby **humanitarian distribution center**, resulting in a high number of casualties.
 
• Local authorities in the **Dnipropetrovsk Oblast** confirmed that the strike occurred during the night, catching many residents asleep and complicating search and rescue efforts led by the **State Emergency Service of Ukraine**.
 
• The **Ukrainian Air Force** reported that while several incoming projectiles were neutralized by **air defense systems**, the volume of the **mid-June** barrage was designed to overwhelm local defenses.
 
• This specific event in **2025** highlighted the ongoing vulnerability of cities located along the **Dnieper River**, which serve as critical nodes for both **military logistics** and **civilian refuge**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dnipro:**
 
 
• It is the **fourth-largest city** in **Ukraine** and acts as the administrative center of the **Dnipropetrovsk Oblast**.
 
• Due to its strategic location on the **Dnieper River**, it has remained a primary target for **Russian forces** throughout the conflict that escalated in **February 2022**.
 
• The city is a major **industrial hub**, known historically for its **aerospace** and **metallurgical industries**.
 
 
 
• **Kharkiv:**
 
 
• Located in **northeastern Ukraine**, just **40 kilometers** from the **Russian border**, it is the country's **second-largest city**.
 
• While it faces daily shelling, the specific deadly strike of **mid-June 2025** mentioned in the context of this report was centered on **Dnipro**.
 
 
 
• **Kyiv:**
 
 
• The **capital city** of **Ukraine**, which is heavily fortified with advanced Western-made **surface-to-air missile (SAM)** systems like the **Patriot**.
 
• Although frequently targeted by **Geran-2 drones** and **hypersonic missiles**, its defense success rate is generally higher than that of regional hubs.
 
 
 
• **Lviv:**
 
 
• Situated in **western Ukraine** near the border with **Poland**, **Lviv** serves as a gateway for **Western military aid** and **humanitarian support**.
 
• Strikes in **Lviv** are less frequent compared to eastern cities but usually target **electrical substations** and **transportation infrastructure**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **International Response:** The **mid-June 2025** attack drew immediate condemnation from the **United Nations (UN)** and the **European Union (EU)**, prompting calls for increased **air defense** transfers to **Ukraine**.
 
• **Casualty Data:** Reports indicated that over **20 civilians** lost their lives, and more than **50 were injured**, making it one of the most lethal single-strike incidents of the **summer 2025** campaign.
 
• **Infrastructure Impact:** The damage to the **energy grid** in **Dnipro** caused temporary **blackouts** affecting approximately **100,000 households**, necessitating urgent repairs by **Ukrenergo** engineers.
</ul

questions.question: Who was awarded the prestigious Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the highest honour in Indian cinema, at the 70th National Film Awards ceremony on 8 October 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mithun Chakraborty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Veteran actor **Mithun Chakraborty** was honored with the **Dadasaheb Phalke Award**, the highest recognition in Indian cinema, during the **70th National Film Awards** ceremony held on **8 October 2024**.
 
• The award was presented by the **President of India**, **Droupadi Murmu**, at **Vigyan Bhawan** in **New Delhi**. **Mithun Chakraborty** is the **54th recipient** of this prestigious award for his massive contribution to the film industry.
 
• The announcement of his selection was made earlier on **September 30, 2024**, by the Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting, **Ashwini Vaishnaw**.
 
• The selection was finalized by a distinguished jury consisting of five members: **Asha Parekh**, **Khushbu Sundar**, and **Vipul Amrutlal Shah**, among others.
 
• **Mithun Chakraborty** made his acting debut in the **1976** film **Mrigayaa**, directed by **Mrinal Sen**, for which he won his first **National Film Award for Best Actor**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Mithun Chakraborty.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dadasaheb Phalke Award:**
 
 
• Instituted in **1969**, the award commemorates **Dhandiraj Govind Phalke**, popularly known as the **Father of Indian Cinema**, who directed India’s first full-length feature film, **Raja Harishchandra**, in **1913**.
 
• The award is presented annually at the **National Film Awards** ceremony by the **Directorate of Film Festivals**, an organization set up by the **Ministry of Information and Broadcasting**.
 
• The first recipient of this award was **Devika Rani**, known as the "First Lady of Indian Cinema," who was honored at the **17th National Film Awards**.
 
• The award comprises a **Swarna Kamal** (Golden Lotus) medallion, a shawl, and a cash prize of **Rs. 15 lakh** (which was increased from Rs. 10 lakh recently).
 
 
 
• **Previous Honorees:**
 
 
• Before Mithun Chakraborty, the **53rd Dadasaheb Phalke Award** was conferred upon veteran actress **Waheeda Rehman** for the year **2021**.
 
• Other notable recipients mentioned in the options include **Amitabh Bachchan**, who received the honor in **2018**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Career and Achievements:**
 
 
• **Mithun Chakraborty** has won **three National Film Awards** in his career: Best Actor for **Mrigayaa** (**1976**), Best Actor for **Tahader Katha** (**1992**), and Best Supporting Actor for **Swami Vivekananda** (**1998**).
 
• He is globally renowned for his role in the **1982** blockbuster **Disco Dancer**, which gained him a massive fan following in countries like the **Soviet Union** and **Africa**.
 
• In **April 2024**, he was also conferred with the **Padma Bhushan**, India's third-highest civilian award, by the **Government of India**.
 
• Known affectionately as **Mithun Da**, he has acted in more than **350 films** across various languages including **Hindi**, **Bengali**, **Odia**, **Bhojpuri**, and **Tamil**.
 
 
</ul
